findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses && so team admins are denied
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. `isTeamAdmin` already matches ADMIN or OWNER memberships, so the conjunction is only true for team OWNERs. Team ADMINs who are neither organizer nor attendee get FORBIDDEN, which contradicts the variable name and the intent. The operator should be `||`, or `isTeamAdmin` alone should be used.

findings.title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive and can be bypassed
findings.body: The `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` entries are lowercased, but the incoming `guest` is compared as-is with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Submitting `Blocked@Example.com` instead of `blocked@example.com` gets past the blacklist, so the address is added as an attendee and emailed. Normalize the guest (e.g. `guest.toLowerCase()`) before comparing.

findings.title: Server-side dedup misses in-request duplicates and differing case
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` only drops guests that exactly (case-sensitively) match an existing attendee. Duplicates inside the request itself are not removed, and the server schema has no uniqueness refinement; the dialog's check is client-only and also case-sensitive. A direct API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]`, or `A@x.com` when `a@x.com` already attends, creates duplicate attendee rows via `createMany` and duplicate emails. Dedupe case-insensitively on the server.

findings.title: Raw `guests` passed to email sender instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the unfiltered input. If the request includes an email that already belongs to an attendee, that existing attendee is treated as new. They then get a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a fresh booking confirmation) instead of the add-guests notification. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

findings.title: EventManager built with the acting user's identity/credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: The handler explicitly allows attendees and team admins/owners, not just the organizer, to add guests. But it builds `EventManager` from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The booking's calendar references belong to the organizer's credentials. When a non-organizer performs the action, the calendar update may fail or not reach the organizer's calendar, so the external event never gets the new attendees. `booking.user.credentials` is fetched in the query but never used. Build the EventManager from the booking organizer.

findings.title: Attendees persisted before calendar update with no rollback; failure leaves inconsistent state
findings.body: The new attendees are committed via `prisma.booking.update` before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs. That call is not wrapped in try/catch. If the calendar update throws, the request returns an error and no emails are sent, yet the guests are already saved in the DB. A retry then fails with `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, because the guests now count as existing attendees. The guests are never notified and the calendar is out of sync.

findings.title: No booking status / time check before adding guests
findings.body: The handler never checks booking status or end time. Through the API, guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED or already-finished bookings, and each new guest gets an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` booking confirmation with a CONFIRMED ICS invite for an event that will not happen. The UI also exposes the action on past bookings, because `bookedActions` is rendered for past confirmed bookings. Reject non-active or past bookings.

findings.title: Unbounded guest list enables mass email sending
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` and no `.min(1)`. Any attendee of a booking (not just the organizer) may call this mutation. A user can submit an arbitrarily large list, which creates that many attendee rows and sends that many emails from the organizer's name and reply-to. This is a spam/abuse vector and can also be costly for the mail provider. Add a reasonable upper bound and dedupe on the server.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event type's disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other booking email helper (location change, reschedule, cancel, etc.) accepts `eventTypeMetadata` and skips host or attendee emails when `disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee` is set. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and always emails the organizer, team members and all attendees. Event types configured to suppress standard emails (e.g. because workflows send custom ones) will still send these.

findings.title: CalendarEvent lacks `team`, so team hosts are never notified
findings.body: `evt` is built without a `team` property. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `calendarEvent.team?.members` loop is therefore dead code. For collective or round-robin team events, co-hosts get no notification that guests were added, unlike the other organizer email flows that populate `team.members`.

findings.title: Recurring rule included in invite although guest is added to a single occurrence
findings.body: `recurringEvent` is taken from the event type, so for a recurring event type the ICS sent to new guests carries an RRULE for the whole series. The guest is only added as an attendee to the single `bookingId` occurrence. This happens when the action is used from the Upcoming tab, where per-occurrence edit actions are shown. The guest's calendar then shows a full series they are not booked into.

findings.title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and can render "undefined: ..."
findings.body: `message` is a template literal and is always a non-empty string, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never uses the fallback. When `err.data` is absent (e.g. a network error), the toast reads `undefined: <message>`.

findings.title: Validation error state is never cleared on success, edit or dismiss
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is only reset by the Cancel button. It stays set after a successful add (`onSuccess` doesn't reset it), while the user edits the fields, and when the dialog is closed via overlay or Esc (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` doesn't reset state). The "Emails must be unique and valid" error therefore persists and reappears the next time the dialog is opened.

findings.title: Hardcoded untranslated tooltip text
findings.body: The tooltip text `"Remove email"` is hardcoded English in a shared UI component that otherwise uses `t(...)`. Non-English users will see English text.
